transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Park, thanks for coming back in to see me. I asked you here because I need to discuss a mistake that was made regarding your imaging from last month.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. Was there something wrong with the scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, the scan itself was fine, but there was an incidental finding. That means the radiologist saw something that wasn't the main reason for the test—a small cyst on your kidney—that needed a follow-up scan in three months just to be safe. The error is that this was written in a separate part of the report, and our team missed it. We didn't schedule that follow-up for you. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess. Is it like, cancer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, based on the report, it looks benign, which means it's not cancerous. But we still need to monitor it. Are you following me on how the communication gap happened?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yeah, I think so. You just missed the note.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. I am sorry for any confusion this caused. We were really busy that week and the system for flagging these findings isn't always clear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I'm a bit shaking. I didn't tell my parents about the scan because I wanted to handle it myself, and now I don't know if I should have. I feel kind of panicked.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you're feeling pretty overwhelmed right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't know if this is normal. Like, do people usually miss things? Am I in trouble?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you're not in trouble at all. But look, I actually have to go in a few minutes for a procedure, so I want to make sure we get through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. But I have a few more questions about the cyst. Like, will it—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: If we can just quickly move to the next steps, that would be better.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel like I'm not really sure what my rights are here. I mean, is this a big deal?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's not a big deal in terms of your health, as it's only been a few weeks. We just need to get the scan done.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess. I just feel really weird about it. I thought everything was handled.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, regarding the plan, we'll just get this sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How do we sort it? Do I need to pay for another one?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll look into getting a new appointment set up. You'll probably get an email or a call from the office.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will that happen? Like, today?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure on the timing. Just stay tuned for an email from the scheduling team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What if I don't get an email? Should I call someone?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sure it'll come through. Let's wrap this up now so I can get to my patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still feel a little dizzy. I don't really know what to tell my parents if I do tell them.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You can just tell them we're scheduling a follow-up. It's really not a problem.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay. I'll just wait for the email then.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Great. Thanks for understanding. See you later.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I actually have to go in a few minutes', 'quickly move to the next steps', 'wrap this up now') and interrupts the patient's question about the cyst.

E.justification: Error named in first turn, used lay language, checked comprehension twice ('Does that make sense so far?', 'Are you following me...'), and avoided false reassurance regarding the need for monitoring.

A.justification: Direct apology used ('I am sorry'), but immediately diluted by excuses regarding being busy and the system not being clear.

R.justification: While the resident names one emotion ('overwhelmed'), they subsequently use generic validation ('I understand') and meet further emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: The plan consists only of placeholders ('look into getting a new appointment', 'stay tuned for an email') with no specific timeline or prevention strategy.
